rows.grounds: The near-identity in luminance is intended: --card was decoupled from the page by chroma, not lightness, so a glass plate reads warm over any backdrop while the page/card surface read stays stable (color-radius.css:60-72). Card-to-page separation is carried by the plate's edge ink (--ink-seam flush, --ink-edge floating) and its cast shadow, never by fill contrast (card/styles.css:50-80). A consumer that paints --card as a bare fill (their HLG grid cell) inherits neither and must draw the separation itself from the same one-ink register; that is the one place they asked for. A fill-luminance separation would move every glass plate in the library and is not wanted. The stale DESIGN.md palette block is a real doc defect that plausibly produced the '≡' reading.
rows.cureShape: ANSWER text: 'Intended. --card and --background are distinct tokens (warm-cream plate vs the page) held at nearly the same lightness on purpose; the separation is the plate's edge and cast, not its fill. Where you paint --card as a bare fill, draw the boundary once from the one-ink register: border 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) calc(var(--ink-seam) * 100%), transparent) for a flush cell, --ink-edge for a raised one — the same rungs <Card> uses.' Doc residue for the manifest lane (openQuestions): DESIGN.md 'Default Color Palette' reprints shadcn values that are false against the bytes.
rows.replyLine: O-32 §2.2 — Your 1.035:1 reproduces, but the two tokens are not the same: --card is hsl(30 85% 96%) and --background is hsl(40 30% 98%) at 8.0.0, 9.0.0 and master. They sit at nearly the same lightness on purpose (the plate was split from the page by warmth, not by lightness), and a Card is separated from the page by its edge rung and its shadow, not by its fill. So this is the explicit ruling you asked for: where you use --card as a bare fill, supply the boundary yourself, once, from our ink register — color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) calc(var(--ink-seam) * 100%), transparent) for a flush cell, --ink-edge for a raised one. Our DESIGN.md 'Default Color Palette' block still prints both as hsl(0 0% 100%); that is our stale doc, and it is being corrected.
